hero.title: Build Your First DApp: from idea to launch checklist
hero.subtitle: Follow one complete project: an on-chain guestbook with a tested contract, a Hardhat deploy script and a wallet-connected web page. Plan, review, calculate costs and write the README, with every lab checked and explained.

faq.q: Does this platform run my code?
faq.a: No. You write and run the code on your own computer with free tools. The platform's labs check your plans, reviews, calculations and documents.
No. Everything uses a local chain and the Sepolia test network with free test ETH.

faq.q: Do I need to know JavaScript?
faq.a: Basic JavaScript helps, and the course explains each line of the code it shows.

activities.title: What does a post cost?
activities.objective: Estimate the gas and cost of posting messages of different lengths.
activities.scenario: Storage is charged by 32-byte slots. A rough teaching model: a post costs 21,000 gas for the transaction, 22,100 gas for each new 32-byte slot of message text, and about 70,000 gas for the other fields and the event. Gas price is 30 gwei and 1 ETH is 250,000 rupees (illustrative).
steps: In C2 work out the slots needed: the message length divided by 32, rounded up with ROUNDUP.
In D2 work out the gas: 21,000 plus slots times 22,100 plus 70,000.
In E2 work out the cost in rupees: gas times the gas price in gwei (B8), divided by a billion, times the ETH price (B9).
Fill down rows 2 to 5.
In B11 find how many times more expensive the longest message is than the shortest: E5 divided by E2.

checks.label: C2 is the slots for 20 bytes
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(B2/32,0)

checks.label: D2 is the gas for the greeting
E2 is the cost in rupees
checks.explain: Gas times price, to ETH, to rupees.

checks.label: D5 is the gas for the long note
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B11 is the ratio

activities.title: How long should the user wait?
activities.objective: Plan how long loading states last and when to show a 'taking longer than usual' message.
activities.scenario: Blocks arrive every 12 seconds on average. After a transaction is sent it usually joins the next block or two. Plan the waiting messages. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B6 work out the typical wait for inclusion: the average block time (B2) times the number of blocks expected (B3).
In B7 work out the time after which to show 'taking longer than usual': twice the typical wait.
In B8 work out the time for the required confirmations: confirmations (B4) times the block time.
In B9 work out the polling checks needed if you check every 4 seconds (B5) until the confirmation time: round up B8 divided by B5.
In B10 show Show hint when the elapsed time (B11) is above B7, else Keep waiting.

checks.label: B6 is the typical wait
B7 is the hint threshold
checks.hint: Try the formula =B6*2 here.

checks.label: B8 is the confirmation time
B9 is the polling checks
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(B8/B5,0)

checks.label: B10 is the message
checks.hint: =IF(B11>B7,"Show hint","Keep waiting")
